strengths: Comprehensive and well-curated benchmark addressing critical gap in MLLM evaluation of spatial understanding with 28K diverse samples across 8 categories, 3 question formats, and multiple modalities

Rigorous dataset construction pipeline with multiple distractor generation strategies and integration of 11 existing datasets, plus SpatialScore-Hard curated through multi-model voting and manual verification

Thorough experimental evaluation of 25 models (1B-78B parameters) revealing clear insights: models handle 2D reasoning (~68% accuracy) but struggle with 3D geometry (homography ~26%, pose estimation ~41%)
Practical tool-based approach (SpatialAgent) with 9 integrated CV tools demonstrates substantial improvements: compact models reach 35-46% on SpatialScore-Hard vs ~15% baseline
Excellent reproducibility practices: detailed appendix with prompts, tool specifications, implementation details, and promise to release code and data
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: VGBench relies on existing 3D datasets, all 9 tools are off-the-shelf models, SpatialScore is dataset integration, and Plan-Execute/ReAct are existing paradigms applied straightforwardly

Fundamental approach limitations: acknowledged by authors that 'current MLLMs still lag behind humans, underscoring need for fundamental architectural innovations'—SpatialAgent is a training-free workaround rather than solving root causes
Insufficient ablation and error analysis: no ablation studies on individual tools, limited systematic analysis of tool failures, no error propagation studies, missing breakdown by failure modes
Limited 3D reasoning capability: benchmark relies on RGB frames, lacks direct point cloud/depth map/surface normal inputs; represents 2D→3D reasoning rather than true 3D spatial understanding

Evaluation methodology concerns: generous δ=2 tolerance threshold (0.5×-2× error), inconsistent evaluation protocols across datasets, incomplete mitigation of data leakage risks, missing inter-annotator agreement metrics

Tool robustness not validated: known issues with depth estimation noise, optical flow on large motion not addressed; no graceful degradation when tools fail; error compounding through multi-step reasoning not analyzed
Limited generalization evidence: all evaluation on benchmark; no validation on real-world embodied AI tasks (stated motivation); unclear if improvements transfer beyond SpatialScore

strengths: Addresses an important and underexplored gap in MLLM evaluation for 3D spatial understanding
Comprehensive benchmark with diverse coverage (28K samples, 8 task categories, multiple modalities and QA formats)
Extensive evaluation across 25 models with clear empirical findings about spatial understanding limitations
Rigorous curation of SpatialScore-Hard subset using voting and manual verification
Exceptional transparency with detailed appendix, promised code/data release, and clear experimental setup
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: VGBench repackages standard CV tasks; SpatialAgent is essentially tool orchestration of existing models with standard prompting techniques
Insufficient analysis of SpatialAgent: missing ablation studies, no investigation of which tools/paradigms contribute to improvements, limited error analysis
Data leakage concerns inadequately addressed; potential overlap with MLLM training data not thoroughly analyzed; no cross-dataset generalization analysis

Experimental design issues: arbitrary choices (δ=2 tolerance, 8 video frames) lack sensitivity analysis; unfair multi-image evaluation (single-frame models); missing statistical rigor (no confidence intervals)
Vague and overstated claims ('most comprehensive benchmark,' 'significant improvements' with 46% hard-set accuracy); lacks insight into why models fail or how to fundamentally improve them
Overly dense presentation (39 pages) with core contributions obscured; insufficient guidance on actionable solutions for practitioners

Missing critical ablations and analyses: no inter-annotator agreement, no distractor quality validation, no analysis of tool accuracy and error propagation, no investigation of when to use Plan-Execute vs ReAct

strengths: Comprehensive and well-motivated benchmark addressing a genuine gap in MLLM evaluation of spatial geometry perception
Methodical construction of VGBench with precise 3D annotations and rigorous distractor generation strategies
Large-scale experimental evaluation of 25 MLLMs with clear insights about 2D vs 3D reasoning gaps and fine-tuning limitations
Thoughtfully curated SpatialScore-Hard subset through multi-model voting and manual verification
SpatialAgent provides practical improvements through effective orchestration of complementary tools and two interpretable reasoning paradigms
Extensive appendix with detailed implementation, prompts, and toolbox specifications supporting reproducibility
Clear presentation of results, qualitative examples, and well-articulated limitations
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty in SpatialAgent—primarily combines existing models (RAFT, SIFT, DepthAnythingV2) via prompt engineering rather than introducing new methods
Insufficient analysis of tool dependency—improvements not decomposed between reasoning capability and tool quality; ablation studies missing
Generous evaluation metrics (δ=2 tolerance permissive; primarily accuracy-based; inconsistent metrics across subsets)
Data leakage concerns inadequately addressed—reliance on public 3D datasets (ScanNet, ScanNet++, CA-1M, WildRGB-D) likely to be in training data
Limited baseline comparisons—no evaluation of fine-tuning MLLMs on spatial tasks or comparison with other multi-agent frameworks
Heterogeneous benchmark design with uneven category distribution and inconsistent task formulations across 12 integrated datasets
Insufficient failure analysis—limited systematic study of error patterns by category, difficulty, or modality
Real-world applicability to embodied AI/autonomous navigation claimed but not empirically validated
